newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Straddles, strangles traded in Railtrack.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Straddles, strangles traded in Railtrack.

text.p: Traded options in Railtrack were busy on Wednesday mainly owing to straddle and strangle trades, dealers said.
Selling puts and calls in this way implies selling option premiums in the hope that the underlying stock will remain fairly stable up to the options expiry date.
Conversely, by buying puts and calls the trader expects the shares to be volatile.
One such deal was to sell 450 June 460 puts and calls at 49p and 13p each, making a net credit of 62p -- which will be the maximum profit at expiry if the partly paid shares are 460p.
The purchaser of Railtrack straddles bought bought 575 December 420 puts and calls at 48p and 54p each.
And short strangles were established by selling 450 September 420 puts at 40p as well as 450 September 500 calls at 15p.
By 1440 GMT, the partly paid shares of the railway networks group were own 1/2p to 419-1/2p. The second installment of 190p per shares is due on June 3.
Elsewhere, in airports authority BAA one broker bought 250 April 500 puts and calls at 3-1/2 and 6-1/2p each and crossed half of these. BAA shares added 7p to 508p.

Over in the FTSE index options, traders showed little interest in establishing new positions in the April and May expiry months owing to uncertainty surrounding the national election -- to be held on May 1.
Instead, traders preferred to make volatility and spread trades for June and December expiry -- although even in these the volume of contracts traded were not very large.
One spread trade involved selling 300 December 4500 calls at 145p and buying 300 December 4700 calls at 75p which will make a maximum profit of 75p if the index is below 4500 at expiry.
